text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a full regression sweep on the Flash/paged fusion selector after the selector change we rolled yesterday. seeing ~18-22% p95 token latency increase on SM90 for long sequences when route -> triton_flashpaged instead of cuda_fused for seq_len >= 2048. attaching inline excerpts from the microbench.
kevin: ouch. do you have the exact config you used? was this on CUDA 12.2 or 12.3 image?
maria: repro steps below.
```
# repro (internal perf harness)
PYTHONPATH=./bench python -m rtperf.run --model redwood-7B --device gpu --kernel-selector=auto --min-seq=512 --max-seq=4096 --batching=dynamic --cuda=12.3 --triton=2.25
```

maria: raw stats (median across 5 runs):
```
sm80/cuda_fused (seq=4096): p50=25ms p95=42ms tokens/s=210
sm90/triton_flashpaged (seq=4096): p50=27ms p95=51ms tokens/s=170
```

deepa: interesting — those numbers point to either extra mem copies in the Triton path or different KV cache layout. any nvprof/hiprofile traces?
maria: yes. perf-bot posted flamegraphs to the perf channel but copied a snippet here. main discrepancy is stalls in memcpy_async -> sync and a lot of small kernel launches around kv-compact.
perf-bot: benchmark summary (from 1867772260): [sm90 image cuda12.3]
- cuda_fused: p95 42ms
- triton_flashpaged: p95 51ms (+21%)
- breakdown: attention kernel time similar, overhead: kernel launch+memcpy ~30% higher on triton path
kevin: that aligns with my local trace — Triton uses multiple smaller kernels for paged fusion and does host-device synchronization after compact ops. on sm80 we saw smaller gap because drivers on that box batch the memcpy better.
ryan: what about the batching heuristic? are we favoring triton_flashpaged for large seqs because of lower token cost at high throughput, but we should consider latency SLOs.
maria: current selector policy: if seq >= 2048 AND batch_size >= 2 -> prefer flashpaged_triton for theoretical cost. selector snippet:
```
if seq_len >= 2048 and est_throughput(batch_size, triton) > est_throughput(batch_size, cuda):
    choice = 'triton_flashpaged'
```

deepa: maybe add a latency_penalty term that prefers cuda_fused when p95 estimate > SLO. also KV cache compaction threshold might be different between implementations — triton compacts more aggressively causing mem churn.
kevin: i can push a quick config change to selector to prefer cuda_fused for p95-sensitive routes. propose a canary: add feature flag `kernel_selector.latency_bias=0.15` (meaning prefer kernel with <=15% higher throughput if latency is lower).
ops-bot: canary rollout note: feature flag will be enabled for 10% traffic in us-west-2 for 1h with automatic rollback if p95 increases >5%.
maria: also found a smaller-but-important regression in KV cache behavior: triton path does per-chunk memcpy to a staging buffer before writing main KV, while cuda_fused writes directly into pre-allocated KV region. that accounts for ~6-8ms of the extra p95 in our runs.
ryan: curious if building Triton kernels with LTO or an alternate cuda toolkit (12.2 vs 12.3) changes launch overhead. can we run a quick rebuild with cuda 12.2 and compare?
perf-bot: queued rebuild+bench job (id: 1867772270). results expected ~20m.
kevin: while that's running, small mitigation: change selector rule to prefer cuda_fused for routes where route.slo_type == latency and seq_len >= 1024. that'll avoid 95%-critical traffic hitting the slower path.
deepa: agree. long-term we should try to: 1) reduce per-chunk memcopies in triton kernel, 2) fuse the compact+write step on Triton if possible, 3) revisit kernel-launch batching inside triton runtime.
maria: i'll open a PR with a selector patch and a ticket for the kernel changes. linking quick notes:
- PR: selector latency_bias canary
- TICKET: TRITON-ATTN-456 optimize kv write path + merge compaction

kevin: thanks — if perf-bot rebuild shows cuda12.2 improves launch overhead we can also try switching base image for triton builds.
perf-bot: rebuild finished: cuda12.2 triton_flashpaged p95=48ms (improvement vs 51ms) — still ~14% worse than cuda_fused.
maria: OK so driver/toolkit helps a bit but not full delta. still want the selector change and a targeted kernel fix.
ryan: for the PR can we include a small unit test that simulates KV compaction cost and asserts selector picks the lower-latency kernel under SLO mode?
maria: yes, i'll add tests and a small canary plan in the PR description.
ops-bot: rolling out kernel_selector.latency_bias=0.15 to 10% in us-west-2 now :rocket:
kevin: :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all. follow-ups: I'll file intra-team notes after canary (if stable we'll flip default for latency routes). Ticket TRITON-ATTN-456 assigned to @deepa for kernel changes.
